title: Non-type template parameters
recap: A non-type template parameter supplies a compile-time value rather than a type. Different values identify different specializations of the template.
Separate configuration known at compilation from data supplied at runtime. Here the factor is compile-time configuration, while each call can scale a different runtime value.
objectives: Implement the stated behavior for multiple inputs.
Run the visible tests and explain one boundary case.
warnings: The function/type interface is fixed, but implementation syntax is your choice.
Do not remove the visible tests; the checker keeps an independent copy.
Respect the stated input domain and lifetime/range rules.
challenge: Implement scaleBy<Factor>(value), multiplying an int value by the compile-time integer Factor. Factor may be positive, zero, or negative. All products fit int. Factor is a template argument, not a runtime function parameter.
hints: Use Factor directly in the body.
Do not add Factor to the function parameter list.
A negative factor is valid in this contract.
